did: The open-question essay on merges waiting in line is published to the cards folder, with the five corrections you agreed to, and home voices and renders it once you deploy this morning. Its five pictures of public GitHub pages couldn't travel through the testing repository, which refuses pictures, so they now reach home the way the app's snips do: a capture you or the coordinator dispatch photographs the pages logged out, refuses a page that doesn't load or asks to sign in, and keeps them a day, and each scene names the capture it came from. Home's half was built alongside by another session, and Studio's renders list now says, in plain words, when an essay's page couldn't be had and what to do. Before publishing, a silent render of the essay with the real capture drew all sixteen scenes with nothing overflowing.

calls.title: How a public page's pictures reach home
options: a capture of their own, keyed by its run, kept a day, each scene naming its run, home holding the pictures until the video is made
a job inside the snips capture, keyed by commit like the snips
keep the pictures a week so home may fetch them late
name the run once for the whole essay rather than per scene
calls.why: A snip is the same every time it is taken, so its capture is keyed by commit; a page is live and taken again is a new picture, so the run is what names it, and each run is kept apart so a later capture never pushes out one an essay still needs (C1420).
calls.undo: Record a call that moves C1420: lengthen the capture's retention or key it by commit, and drop the run from a page scene.

left: #3395 stays open until home renders this essay with its pages: that is its definition of done, and it can't be seen until you deploy home.
The capture's pictures expire on 2026-11-24 at 06:53 UTC; if home isn't deployed and fetching by then, the essay is refused and needs a fresh capture with the cut list filled again.

Studio's words for a page home couldn't get don't single out one rare cause, two captures holding the same file differently; the advice they give, to take the pages again and name only the new pictures, still fixes it.
